newsitem.title: USA: CFX Corp. to acquire Portsmouth Bank.
newsitem.headline: CFX Corp. to acquire Portsmouth Bank.

text.p: CFX Corp. said Thursday it has agreed to acquire Portsmouth Bank Shares Inc., which owns Portsmouth Savings Bank in Portsmouth, N.H., for about $106 million in stock.
CFX, which is based in Keene, N.H., also said it will take a special charge of about $2.9 million for one-time costs of the transaction after it is completed.

"Increased penetration into higher growth markets has been a strategic objective of CFX and Portsmouth is a natural extension of our current banking system," CFX President Peter J. Baxter said in a statement.
The company said that under the definitive agreement each outstanding common share of Portsmouth will be converted into .95 share of CFX common stock.

CFX, a bank holding company, said that, based on the $18.50 closing price of its common stock Wednesday, the indicated value of the deal would be $17.58 for each Portsmouth share, putting the total value of the deal at about $106 million.
Both companies' stock fell after the news. CFX lost 87.5 cents to $17.625 on the American Stock Exchange while Portsmouth slipped 25 cents to $15.50 on Nasdaq.
CFX, which also owns two banks in Massachusetts, said that three Portsmouth directors will join the CFX board and two will become directors of CFX Bank.
It added that the transaction, which is expected to be tax-free to the shareholders of Portsmouth, is subject to regulatory approval and the approval of both CFX's and Portsmouth's shareholders.

If the average price of CFX common stock for the 10 trading days preceding the last regulatory approval required for the transaction is below $15.70, the exchange ratio becomes 1.05 shares, the company said.
The exchange ratio would float between .95 and 1.05 shares if the average price of CFX common is between $17.375 to and $15.70.
